delay.comparison: Every output sample from frame zero at the same frame; no alignment, warmup exclusion, envelope substitution or frequency-only qualification.
delay.channel_counts: Both connected source outputs and both native outputs must be exactly mono; unused native storage must be numerical zero.
delay.finite: Every visible and padded output value must be finite.
delay.signed_zero: Positive and negative zero are numerically equivalent; no bitwise zero-sign requirement.
delay.justification: Fixed 2 mV absolute plus 10 ppm relative permits ordinary f32 platform math differences while requiring startup, timing, feedback, tone and mix to remain pointwise close. Long feedback traces receive the identical bound.

resampler.counts: input_frames_used and output_frames_gen must match on every individual process call, including calls producing no output.
resampler.comparison: Compare every emitted output at identical call and offset, with persistent state and no reset except a declared new scenario; end_of_input always false.
resampler.justification: Direct SRC qualification removes the delay feedback loop as a possible source of count or interpolation errors. Fixed 2 micro-unit absolute plus 2 ppm relative is stricter than the whole-module voltage bound.

history_wrap: 2,200,000 frames exceeds the 2^21 logical ring position. It exercises repeated physical wrap under ordinary short delay, and does not claim the history queue can become full at the supported 10-second delay.
lifecycle: Parameter changes rebuild the native module and adopt the prior state. A separate explicit adoption case rebuilds with unchanged parameters at non-buffer-aligned frame numbers. The source class continues untouched across those events.
scope: Actual pinned Delay class prefix with only plugin.hpp replaced by rack.hpp; actual SDK src_new/src_process SRC_SINC_FASTEST. Bypass, host graph/cable timing, finite-voltage policy and sample-rate rebuilds require separate host tests and are not qualified by the DSP oracle.
